text:
marie: Heads-up — after rolling the continuous-batcher heuristic change (cb-heuristic-v3) at ~10:41 we're seeing 99p latency spikes and overall throughput drop on prod-gpu. Anyone watching? :eyes:
InfraBot: deploy completed by marie at 2026-01-06T10:41:02Z - canary -> 100% - change_id=cb-heuristic-v3
dave: Saw it on staging too. 99p went from ~220ms -> ~1.6s and QPS down ~18%. Dash shows a lot more small batches forming.
priya: Adding a profiler dump now. Quick q: did we change the pack_by_latency thresholds or token_budget_target?
marie: Yes — token_budget_target moved 128 -> 64 and pack_by_latency_ms default set to 32 to tighten tail latency.
dave: Rolled config snippet we used:
```json
{"continuous_batching": {"token_budget_target": 64, "pack_by_latency_ms": 32, "queue_policy": "tail_latency_pref"}}
```
priya: Profiler (condensed): attention_kv_lookup -> kernel_conv_fp32 -> kernel_dispatch_slow. Lots of fallback to fp32 kernels for small shapes. kernel-miss-rate ~37%.
marie: I also noticed kv_cache hitrate in the hour after deploy dropped from ~92% -> ~48%. Example logs:
"[2026-01-06T10:42:11Z] kv_cache: evict key=prefix-1 size=4096 reason=cache_pressure"
"[2026-01-06T10:43:05Z] kv_cache: hit=false key=prefix-7"
dave: Cache thrash explains more recompute and changes in the shape distribution. If prefixes are not reused we get many tiny seqs and kernel selector chooses a slower path.
jen-sre: Pinging routing/infra — any chance fallback routing kicked more requests to cpu-backed nodes when kernels mismatched?
priya: Perf counters summary (before -> after):
"batch_count: 24500 -> 18700"
"avg_batch_size: 18 -> 8"
"kernel_dispatch_fp16: 64% -> 38%"
"kernel_dispatch_fp32_fallback: 3% -> 29%"
marie: Kernel-level latency shift:
"P50 total: 180ms -> 240ms"
"P95 attention_kv_lookup: 10ms -> 95ms"
dave: Hypothesis: lowering token_budget_target increased join-churn which created more small batches and increased cache pressure. That reduces prefix reuse and forces fallback to slower kernels -> higher tail latency and reduced throughput.
priya: Repro loadgen command we used to validate locally:
```bash
# simulate traffic skewed to short continuations
./loadgen --seq-dist "mostly-short" --continuation-rate 0.6 --hosts prod-canary
```
dave: Mitigation options: revert token_budget_target -> 128, or change queue_policy to favor batch size over strict tail-latency, or increase KV cache capacity.
marie: Can we try bumping kv_cache size + pin token_budget to 128 on canary while we collect traces?
jen-sre: Rolling temporary change: kv_cache.max_entries x2 on prod-canary and pin token_budget_target=128 for 10m.
InfraBot: kv_cache config change applied to prod-canary by jen-sre at 2026-01-06T10:52:15Z
priya: Early post-change metrics (10m window): hitrate climbed -> 85%, avg_batch_size -> 15, throughput +12%, P95 down ~400ms.
dave: I'll run nvprof + kernel-dispatch logs for a longer window. Also propose adding a soft pack_by_batch_size constraint so we don't over-optimize for tail latency at the expense of kernel efficiency.
marie: Action items: (1) revert token_budget_target globally? (2) add cache-growth + softer eviction policy; (3) instrument kernel-selection-switch metric and pack-by-batch soft constraint. Owners: marie/dave/priya. I'll open a follow-up ticket and attach traces.
marie: Thanks all :heart:
dave: Nice recovery — thanks jen-sre and priya. :thumbsup:
